historical_references.reference: Asavari was a queen consort of the Maurya Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (c. 321-297 BCE) and is believed to have been the mother of Bindusara, who succeeded his father as the emperor.

Asavari was a daughter of the Ikshvaku king Dharma, and was married to the Satavahana king Rudradaman I (130-150 CE). She is known for her patronage of Buddhism and for constructing the rock-cut caves at Bhaja and Karla, which are important sites in the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit in Maharashtra.

Asavari, also known as 'Shrubhaka' or 'Brahmi', is a revered herb used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine for its numerous health benefits. In the context of modern trends, Asavari is seen on various platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and blogs, where it is featured in Ayurvedic skincare routines, herbal remedies, and wellness industry discussions. Instagram accounts dedicated to Ayurvedic living often showcase Asavari as a key ingredient in homemade skincare products, while YouTube videos provide tutorials on how to use Asavari for hair growth and as a brain tonic. Overall, the modern context of 'Asavari' reflects a growing interest in natural remedies and holistic wellness practices.
